figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
FIG. 1.
Outline of the Taxol biosynthetic pathway. The cyclization of geranylgeranyl diphosphate to taxadiene by taxadiene synthase and
the hydroxylation (with allylic rearrangement) of taxadiene to taxadien-5a-ol by the 5a-hydroxylase are illustrated. Either taxadienol or the
corresponding 5a-acetate, formed by the C5-O-acetyl transferase, serves as the intermediate for subsequent oxygenation and acyl transfer
steps on route to Taxol by a series of largely undeﬁned enzymatic reactions (large open arrow).

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
FIG. 4.
Mass spectrometric analyses of (A) the HPLC-puriﬁed principal metabolite (peak 2 of Fig. 3A) derived from taxadienol by Taxus
microsomes optimized for cytochrome P450-mediated oxygenation, and of (B) the HPLC-puriﬁed principal metabolite (peak 12 of Fig. 3B,
following alkaline hydrolysis) derived from taxadienyl acetate by the same microsomal system. The two spectra are not only discernibly
different in the distribution of fragment ions but the two metabolites also differ in GC retention time by nearly 2 min.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 5
figure_candidates.caption:
FIG. 5.
Time courses of taxadienol hydroxylase (A) and taxadiene hydroxylase (B) activities measured in microsomal preparations of
untreated (control) T. cuspidata suspension cell cultures and cultures following induction with methyl jasmonate. Taxadienol hydroxylase
activities in noninduced (F) and induced (}) cells are plotted in A; the time courses of taxadienyl acetate hydroxylase activities in noninduced
and induced cells were similar to those of the corresponding taxadienol hydroxylase activities. As an additional control for a cytochrome P450
oxygenase that is not substantially inducible by methyl jasmonate, the corresponding time courses for taxadiene hydroxylase activities in
noninduced (F) and induced (}) cells are plotted in B. The 0-h time point corresponds to the enzyme activities from cells harvested
immediately prior to methyl jasmonate addition.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 6
figure_candidates.caption:
FIG. 6.
NMR spectra (in deutero-benzene) of the biosynthetic product derived from taxadien-5a-ol in Taxus cell microsomal preparations.
(A) 1H-NMR spectrum (scaled along the X-axis from 0.5 ppm to 5.3 ppm); (B) 2D-1H[13C]/13C HSQC; (C) 2D-1H/1H homonuclear TOCSY; (D)
2D-1H/1H homonuclear ROESY. Note that the NMR pattern expected for H20 from the
13C–1H isotopomer is collapsed in the ROESY
spectrum as a result of continuous low power 13C-decoupling applied during the experiment. This procedure increased the intensity of the
cross-peaks arising from interactions with protons at C20 (H20) by about 75%.
